Article Title: SIR row: Will annul Election Commission orders not in keeping with law, says Supreme Court
Article Text:
‘Decisions must be unanimous or by majority’, says Supreme Court

CEC, ECs need to either rebut or endorse allegations about ‘unilateral decisions’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Monday asked the Election Commission , CEC Gyanesh Kumar and ECs S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi to clarify whether crucial decisions regarding the special intensive revision (SIR) of voter rolls were taken unilaterally by the CEC, and said it would injunct (bar) those decisions by the three-member commission which were neither unanimous nor by majority.A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said irrespective of powers vested in the CEC, the law clearly mandates that all decisions must either be by unanimity or by majority among the three members of the EC. “If we come across instances (where CEC has unilaterally taken decisions), we will annul them,” it said.The statement came after senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for a PIL petitioner, strongly argued for an interim direction to the EC to only take decisions by unanimity during pendency of the petition as the amended CEC and Other ECs (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, gave the CEC enormous powers.The PIL has sought scrutiny of the validity of SIR decisions and ”alterations” in Form 6 for new voters. Singh said since the court could not undo elections, a direction must be issued that in the interregnum, EC must follow the statutory mandate. He pleaded that EC be directed to preserve all records on SIR decisions and Form 6 alteration and produce them before SC for scrutiny.Let us have some authenticated facts before us through their responses.They must respond in a clear and transparent manner. If the records show some of the decisions are not taken by majority, we will injunct those. But we cannot put the cart before the horse, the bench said while also issuing notices to the Centre, deputy EC Manish Garg and EC’s director general (IT) Seema Khanna.This has set the stage for the CEC and, more crucially, the two ECs to either endorse or rebut the allegation that important decisions on SIR were taken by Gyanesh Kumar unilaterally and in violation of the law which lays down that the commission’s calls are to be made either unanimously or, failing that, by majority. The allegation, based on a newspaper report, is at the core of the controversy which has reignited opposition to SIR.Senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for a PIL petitioner, also questioned the validity of Section 16 of the 2023 Act, which provided that “no court shall entertain or continue any civil or criminal proceedings against any person who is, or was, a CEC or an election commissioner for any act, thing or word, committed, done or spoken by him when, or in the course of acting or purporting to act in the discharge of his official duty or function”.He said this was way beyond the immunity enjoyed even by SC judges and especially when it was not extended even to the PM.Justice Bagchi said, “We will examine the expression ‘or was’. Protection while in office is understandable. Such protection (as provided under Section 16) is perhaps only with regard to the President. It is not given to constitutional court judges under Judges Inquiry Act.”Singh pleaded for suspension of the CEC or divesting him of his authority. When the bench asked who would conduct elections, Singh said the other two ECs would do it. He said in the interim, the SC-mandated selection panel for CEC should be brought back in which the CJI is included along with the PM and the LoP. The 2023 Act replaced the CJI with a Union minister nominated by the PM.When the bench declined, Singh said the situation was so grave that it could undermine the very basis of our democracy. “Today, the CEC is acting in a manner which is contrary to the statute under which he is appointed. Court should pass some interim orders (restraining the CEC from discharging his functions), otherwise the country will burn,” he said.Patna-based petitioner Rakesh Kumar Singh has sought a direction to EC to “produce before SC the complete original and primary records relating to the matters pleaded herein, including minutes, agendas, approvals, file notings, work allocation and delegation orders, IT-access records, server logs, audit trails and database-change histories concerning the functioning of the commission, ERONet/EClNet, alteration of Form 6 and filing of appeals before the Bengal appellate tribunals”.
Article Summary: Supreme Court asks the Election Commission to clarify whether crucial decisions were taken unilaterally by the CEC. A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said the law clearly mandates that all decisions must either be by unanimity or by majority among the three members of the EC. “If we come across instances (where CEC has unilaterally taken decisions), we will annul them,” it said.

Article Title: National Commission for Women seeks gender-neutral childcare leave, shared caregiving by parents
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Noting that “motherhood should not become a career penalty”, National Commission for Women (NCW) has called for measures to prevent recruitment discrimination against women arising from maternity, as part of a slew of recommendations to govt on laws related to maternity and childcare.In a report — containing 37 recommendations — NCW has also called for a shift to shared caregiving by transforming existing women-centric child care legal framework into gender-neutral child care leave, available to either parent. The commission batted for extension of “gender neutral” child care leave to private sector, mandatory paid paternity leave, expanding childcare leave eligibility to include third child through graded model, and highlighted the urgent need to make room for 5 lakh creches by 2030.It called for maternity protection to reach women beyond the formal workforce, and recommended extending maternity and childcare benefits to informal, gig and platform workers, noting that over 90% of women workers remain outside effective coverage.NCW has submitted its recommendations to the department of personnel and training (DoPT) and women and child development and labour and employment ministries, with a focus on strengthening India’s maternity and childcare framework through shared parenting, universal maternity protection and family-friendly workplaces.It further recommended parity in maternity benefits for biological, adoptive and commissioning mothers, including increasing leave for adoptive and commissioning mothers from 12 weeks to 26 weeks. It also called for amending Section 60(4) of Social Security Code, 2020, in light of the Supreme Court ruling concerning adoptive mothers, while advocating for a child-centric caregiving framework rather than distinctions based solely on biological motherhood.NCW proposed dividing the existing 730-day child care leave structure equally between both working parents, with 365 days each, or allowing a common pool where both parents work in the same organisation. For children aged 0–2 years, it further proposes a 60:40 shared-care model between primary and secondary caregivers.The commission has also proposed extending child care leave to private-sector employees through a phased implementation model, beginning with large industries and subsequently covering medium and small enterprises.
Article Summary: National Commission for Women (NCW) has called for measures to prevent recruitment discrimination against women arising from maternity. NCW has also called for a shift to shared caregiving by transforming existing women-centric child care legal framework into gender-neutral child care leave, available to either parent.

Article Title: Visa doesn't create absolute right to enter India, says Delhi High Court
Article Text:
File photo

Poll Vote & Share your view How important do you think national security is in determining entry to a country? Very important Somewhat important Not important at all 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Delhi High Court has stressed that a foreign national does not have an inherent or legally enforceable right to seek entry into India even if granted a visa. It added the statutory framework does not treat the possession of a visa as creating an absolute and unconditional right of admission into India.Justice Amit Mahajan observed: "The statutory scheme expressly contemplates circumstances in which, notwithstanding possession of requisite travel documents, a foreigner may not be permitted to enter India on grounds, including considerations relating to national security, sovereignty and integrity of India, relations with a foreign State and public health, besides others specified by central govt.""The claim is destined to fail because there is no inherent or legally enforceable right of a foreign national to seek entry," he added. High Court's observations came while dismissing a plea by a Turkmenistan woman, seeking a direction to Centre to furnish a written speaking order giving the reasons for refusing her entry on March 25.
Article Summary: Delhi High Court says a foreign national does not have an inherent or legally enforceable right to seek entry into India even if granted a visa. High Court's observations came while dismissing a plea by a Turkmenistan woman, seeking a direction to Centre to furnish a written speaking order.

Article Title: Only 15% going to work use public transport: NSO
Article Text:
Walking is the 2nd most common mode of work commute

28.3% of people reach workplace on foot: NSO

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Long traffic snarls, a common feature on roads across the country, may be linked to how people commute to work. Only 15% of workers use public transport such as buses, trains, trams or auto-rickshaws, while 46% rely on two-wheelers or cars, according to the first-ever National Household Travel Survey (NHTS) by the National Statistics Office (NSO).Two-wheelers account for 43% of workers' commute nationally and cars for 3%. In urban areas, reliance on these vehicles is higher, with 53% of workers using two-wheelers and 5.7% travelling by car.Walking is the second most common mode of work commute in the country, accounting for 28.3% of workers, 10.7% use bicycles. More than a third of rural workers (36%) walk to work, compared with just 14% in urban areas, as per the data. The survey was conducted between July 2025 and June 2026 and included trips which are longer than 1 km. Travelling to and fro has been counted as two trips in the survey.The survey showed a worker takes an average of 25 minutes to reach the workplace. In urban areas, the commute takes 27 minutes, compared with 23 minutes in rural areas. The morning commute remains heavily concentrated before 10 am, with nearly 95% of workers leaving home for work then.In terms of cost, workers spend an average of Rs 785 a month on commuting, with men spending substantially more (Rs 835) than women (Rs 533). The gap widens further in rural areas, where men spend more than twice as much as women — Rs 674 against Rs 307.In contrast, student mobility shows a markedly different pattern. Walking is the single largest mode, accounting for 37% of students travelling to educational institutions, followed by buses at 29.5% and bicycles at 15.8%. Around 88% reach their institutions within 30 minutes, while the average journey takes 23 minutes. Nearly four in five students leave for school between 7 am and 10 am.Besides meeting the railway ministry’s specific data requirements, the survey is expected to provide insights into how, when and why people travel. “Information on travel patterns and public transport use will help identify gaps in existing transport systems, assess accessibility, optimise routes and improve service frequency and scheduling,” said NSO in a statement.
Article Summary: Only 15% of workers use public transport such as buses, trains, trams or auto- rickshaws. More than a third of rural workers (36%) walk to work, compared with just 14% in urban areas. Workers spend an average of Rs 785 a month on commuting.

NEW DELHI: Union law ministry Monday notified appointment of three judges for Supreme Court, taking the total strength of the apex court to 37 judges, including Chief Justice of India , against a sanctioned strength of 38 judges. The new judges will take oath of office likely Tuesday.The three new judges for SC are Justice Sunita Agarwal, currently Chief Justice of Gujarat High Court; Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya, Chief Justice of Delhi High Court; and Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh, Chief Justice of Telangana High Court.The three chief justices were recommended for elevation to the apex court on Sept 28 by the SC collegium, comprising of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Vikram Nath, B V Nagarathna, M M Sundresh and P S Narasimha.Justice Agarwal will be the third woman judge in SC with Justices B V Nagarathna and V Mohana, the other two currently on the bench. While Justices Agarwal and Upadhyay come from the same parent HC of Allahabad, Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh's parent HC is Jharkhand.With the latest appointments, Allahabad High Court has four representations on SC bench, the others include Justices Vikram Nath, who will be the next CJI in Feb, and Justice Manoj Mishra.Justice Agarwal and Justice Upadhyay were appointed judges of Allahabad HC in Nov 2011 while Justice Singh was appointed judge of Jharkhand HC in Jan 2012. Justice Agarwal became CJ of Gujarat HC in July 2023. Justice Upadhyay was appointed CJ of Bombay HC on July 29, 2023 and then CJ of Delhi HC on Jan 21, 2025.The law ministry also notified appointment of Saket court judicial officer Gurvinder Pal Singh as additional judge of Delhi HC, a two year tenure before an additional judge is confirmed as permanent judge of the HC.
Article Summary: The new judges will take oath of office likely Tuesday. Justice Sunita Agarwal will be the third woman judge in SC with Justices B V Nagarathna and V Mohana, the other two currently on the bench. Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh come from the same parent HC of Allahabad.

NEW DELHI: Election Commission officials said Monday Form 6 had not been changed; only an additional declaration form had been introduced under the SIR documentation framework, to accompany it.The clarification followed CJI Surya Kant's observation that "any modified Form 6 has not been approved by us".This had led LoP Rahul Gandhi to accuse CEC Gyanesh Kumar of changing Form 6 "illegally and unilaterally".EC called Gandhi's statement misleading and said his citation of its September 26 press note ignored paragraph 1(iii), which referred only to Supreme Court having upheld the declaration attached to Form 6. It said Bihar's June 24-2025 SIR order and the September 26 note had full commission approval.SIR orders for Bihar on June 24-2025, 12 states and UTs on Oct 27-2025, and 19 states and UTs on May 14-2026 required applicants to file annexure D with Form 6/8 to support its declaration. EC said all SIR decisions had unanimously been approved by CEC and both election commissioners.Sources said SC's May 27-2026 order acknowledged that new voters had to submit Form 6 with annexure D. It held Bihar's SIR neither conflicted with RP Act and Registration of Electors Rules, nor undermined free and fair polls, and called the documentation regime a considered exercise of EC's administrative discretion towards its constitutional mandate. They said the declaration form was introduced to ease compliance because filers needed no other document.On September 29, EC dropped the additional declaration requirement in states and UTs where SIR was completed or is yet to start.
Article Summary: Election Commission officials say Form 6 had not been changed. Only an additional declaration form had been introduced under the SIR documentation framework. LoP Rahul Gandhi had accused CEC Gyanesh Kumar of changing Form 6 "illegally and unilaterally"

Article Title: Dibrugarh's river trade returns after 70 years: First post-Independence cargo from Assam heads to Bangladesh
Article Text:
Vessel flagged off for voyage

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Dibrugarh on Monday resumed international river trade after nearly seven decades, with Union Shipping Minister Sarbananda Sonowal flagging off a barge carrying 540 metric tonnes of methanol from Bogibeel Terminal to Dhaka, marking the first cargo shipment from upper Assam to a foreign port since Independence.The methanol, produced by state-owned Assam Petro-Chemicals Ltd (APCL) at Namrup, will travel around 768 km along National Waterway-2 on the Brahmaputra before reaching the India-Bangladesh border and continuing through the Indo-Bangladesh Protocol Route. The voyage from Bogibeel to Narayanganj in Bangladesh will cover around 1,300 km.The shipment is being seen as a test of the Brahmaputra's potential as a commercially viable freight corridor connecting the Northeast with overseas markets. Regular methanol shipments to Bangladesh are planned, with the movement enabled by recently established customs and immigration facilities at Bogibeel and Dhubri.The voyage also revives Dibrugarh's river trade nearly 70 years after its historic river ghat shut down. The ghat closed in 1956 as tea shipments shifted to rail, ending regular river bookings from the town.“Our grandparents grew up hearing the steamer whistle at Dibrugarh Ghat.For 70 years, that whistle fell silent and the ships stopped coming,” Sonowal said. “Today, a ship leaves Dibrugarh for the world once again. The river never failed us. What it lacked for decades was the will to revive it.”The vessel DLB Patkai, pushed by the tug Kushal Konwar, will carry the cargo to Pangaon Port in Dhaka. Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma joined the flag-off ceremony virtually.Sarma described the shipment as a significant moment for the state, saying, “Assam's own product, made in Namrup, is now traveling to an international market on Assam's own river. The Northeast is no longer a frontier. It is India's gateway to the East.”The revival of Dibrugarh's river connectivity has been supported by the Bogibeel passenger and cargo terminal, which opened in February 2024, along with customs and immigration infrastructure and the Jalvahak cargo incentive programme.The route has seen growing activity in recent years. Tata Steel barges reached Pandu through Bangladesh in February 2022, while the river cruise vessel MV Ganga Vilas travelled from Varanasi to Dibrugarh through Bangladesh in 2023.The government is also seeking to expand inland waterways as an alternative freight network. Cargo movement on India's national waterways rose from 18 million metric tonnes in 2013-14 to 218 million metric tonnes in 2025-26, according to the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways.More than Rs 6,800 crore is being invested in waterways across the Northeast, including the development of National Waterway-2, a ship repair facility at Pandu and last-mile connectivity to Pandu Port.Sonowal said the economic and environmental case for waterways was also significant. “Every ton we move on the river means less fuel burnt and fewer trucks on the highway,” he said.The government is working with Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan and Myanmar to develop regional waterway links, with the Dibrugarh-Dhaka shipment potentially opening another freight route for products from the Northeast to international markets.
Article Summary: First cargo shipment from upper Assam to a foreign port since Independence. The shipment is being seen as a test of the Brahmaputra's potential as a commercially viable freight corridor. The voyage also revives Dibrugarh's river trade nearly 70 years after its historic river ghat shut down.

Article Title: Uttarakhand CM Dhami hands over appointment letters to 332 recruits under ESI scheme
Article Text:

Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Monday distributed appointment letters to 332 newly recruited personnel, including 271 appointees in the AYUSH Department and 61 Allopathic Pharmacy Officers under the Employees' State Insurance (ESI) Scheme, at an event held at the Mukhya Sevak Sadan at the Chief Minister's Camp Office.Congratulating the newly appointed personnel, Dhami urged them to discharge their responsibilities with a strong sense of service, sensitivity and dedication.The Chief Minister said receiving an appointment letter marks an important milestone in the lives of young people and also marks the beginning of a new responsibility towards public service.He urged the new recruits not to view government service merely as a job, but as an opportunity to bring positive change to the lives of people at the grassroots.He said the role of personnel associated with the AYUSH Department and the ESI Scheme is directly linked to people's health and well-being."People travelling from remote areas to government health centres and hospitals do so with faith in the system. The sensitivity, promptness and efficiency of government personnel further strengthen this trust," Dhami said, urging the recruits to set an example through their work wherever they are posted.He said every person visiting a hospital or health centre arrives with hope, and the right decision and sincere efforts of healthcare personnel can make a significant difference to the lives of those in need.Dhami said the state government has taken effective steps to make the recruitment system transparent and fair. Along with stringent action against cheating mafias, a strict anti-copying law has also been implemented.He said Uttarakhand's youth are now getting opportunities in government services on the basis of their hard work and merit. More than 35,000 youths have secured government jobs over the past five years, he said, adding that this reflects the government's commitment to a transparent recruitment system.The Chief Minister said Uttarakhand, besides being known as Devbhoomi, has a rich tradition of yoga, Ayurveda and medicinal herbs. The state government is working continuously to develop Uttarakhand as a model 'AYUSH State' and a 'Global Wellness Hub'.He said AYUSH services are being expanded across all districts, Panchakarma services are being modernised, and Ayurveda Centres of Excellence are being established.Through e-Sanjeevani, people are also being provided access to specialist consultations from home, while the 'AYUSH Setu Portal' is another important initiative in this direction.Several homestays across the state have also been linked with wellness services at nearby Ayurvedic hospitals, he said, adding that the government aims to provide visitors to Uttarakhand with a better experience of health and mental well-being through yoga, Ayurveda and Panchakarma.Dhami said healthcare services under the ESI Scheme are also being expanded continuously. Earlier, the scheme was operational in six districts of the state and has now been extended to all 13 districts.A 100-bed ESI hospital has started functioning in Rudrapur, while construction of a 300-bed ESI hospital is underway in Haridwar. Land has also been identified for an ESI hospital in Kashipur. The recruitment process for 47 new medical officers is in its final stage, he added.The Chief Minister said the state government is committed to providing better and accessible healthcare facilities to every person.He expressed confidence that the energy and capabilities of the newly recruited personnel would play an important role in fulfilling the vision of a developed and empowered Uttarakhand.AYUSH Education Minister Madan Kaushik also congratulated the newly appointed personnel and said the state government is continuously working to strengthen and make AYUSH services more accessible to the people.He said the induction of the new personnel would enhance the department's efficiency and further strengthen AYUSH healthcare services across the state.He also urged them to discharge their duties with dedication, sensitivity and a spirit of service and play an active role in providing better healthcare to the public.
Article Summary: Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Monday distributed appointment letters to 332 newly recruited personnel. He urged the new recruits not to view government service merely as a job, but as an opportunity to bring positive change to the lives of people at the grassroots. More than 35,000 youths have secured government jobs over the past five years.

Article Title: Supreme Court pauses coercive action against Tata Chemicals in marine sanctuary case
Article Text:
The dispute relates to the Tata's Mithapur facility in Gujarat.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday directed that no coercive action be taken against Tata Chemicals while it considers the company's challenge to a Gujarat high court ruling concerning alleged environmental damage to a marine sanctuary in the Gulf of Kutch.A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued notice on Tata Chemicals' plea against the high court's May 25 judgment. The bench asked the Gujarat government to respond by November 2."Meanwhile, no coercive action shall be taken against the petitioners," the Supreme Court said according to news agency PTI.Senior advocate Abhishek Singhvi, representing Tata Chemicals, told the court that the case concerns allegations of environmental degradation and encroachment.The dispute relates to the company's Mithapur facility, where open channels have historically been used to discharge wastewater into the sea. Tata Chemicals had challenged a 2006 order passed by the district collector, who rejected the company's claim over the land on which these channels were located.The Gujarat high court dismissed that challenge on May 25. It also rejected Tata Chemicals' argument that it had pre-existing rights over the legacy open wastewater channels.The high court found that government land forming part of the marine sanctuary had been encroached upon. It further directed the Gujarat Pollution Control Board to appoint experts to assess the environmental damage caused to the area.The experts have also been asked to recommend suitable measures to restore or remedy the damage and determine the compensation that may be payable. The exercise was directed to be completed within three months.The Supreme Court's order means that no coercive steps will be taken against Tata Chemicals for the time being as the court examines the company's challenge to the Gujarat high court judgment.
Article Summary: The dispute relates to the Tata's Mithapur facility in Gujarat. Tata Chemicals had challenged a 2006 order passed by the district collector. The Gujarat high court dismissed that challenge on May 25. The high court found that government land forming part of the marine sanctuary had been encroached upon.

Article Title: 'What's the purpose of SIR if citizens are removed?' Bombay high court's Goa bench raps EC
Article Text:
A Bombay high court bench raised concerns over the Election Commission's handling of the SIR.

Maharashtra HC declines urgent intervention

Petition seeks safeguards before voter deletion

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Bombay high court's Goa bench on Monday "reminded" the Election Commission of India (ECI) that "it has an obligation to ensure that eligible Indian citizens are included" in the final electoral roll, questioning the purpose of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) if voters are being removed from the list."But what are you doing? If citizens are being removed from the list then what is the purpose of this entire SIR process?" a division bench of Justices Valmiki Menezes and Amit Jamsandekar, was quoted as saying by Live Law.The court's remarks came while examining concerns over voter deletions during the SIR exercise. The bench referred to observations made by the Supreme Court that ensuring the inclusion of Indian citizens in the final voter list is the ECI's responsibility.The comments was in the backdrop of the wider legal challenge to the voter revision exercise, with concerns being raised over the manner in which names could be excluded from electoral rolls.Meanwhile, the Bombay high court's principal bench in Mumbai refused to pass an urgent interim order stopping the deletion of voters' names in Maharashtra under the SIR process.A bench comprising Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna said the issue was already before the Supreme Court and that it would not be appropriate for the high court to conduct parallel proceedings or issue orders on the matter.The court was hearing a petition filed by Sagar Ramesh Gawai, youth wing president of the Vanchit Bahujan Aghadi, founded by former MP Prakash Ambedkar The petition alleges procedural violations and arbitrary exclusion of voters during the door-to-door enumeration exercise being carried out as part of the SIR in Maharashtra. It has also sought greater transparency and compliance with provisions of the Representation of the People Act.The petitioner has opposed unilateral deletion of names from electoral rolls and sought a formal hearing before an Electoral Registration Officer, followed by a reasoned or speaking order, before any voter is removed.Senior advocate Ashutosh Kumbhakoni, appearing for the ECI, told the court that the Supreme Court is scheduled to hear the SIR matter concerning Maharashtra and other states and Union Territories on October 8.The high court said it would amount to judicial impropriety to examine the same issue simultaneously. It also noted that the Supreme Court had specifically requested High Courts not to conduct parallel proceedings concerning the SIR exercise.Prakash Ambedkar, appearing for the petitioner, sought an interim direction preventing any further deletion of names from the electoral rolls. The high court declined to grant the relief at this stage and posted the matter for hearing after three weeks.
Article Summary: Bombay high court's Goa bench "reminded" Election Commission of India that "it has an obligation to ensure that eligible Indian citizens are included" The bench referred to observations made by the Supreme Court that ensuring the inclusion of Indian citizens in the final voter list is the ECI's responsibility. The court's remarks came while examining concerns over voter deletions.

Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

IMD alert for Tuesday

South India forecast

Article Title: Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta poses for a group picture during an on-site inspection of waste disposal operations near Okhla, in New Delhi

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

New processing plants at three sites

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view What is your top concern regarding pollution in Delhi? Landfill waste Air quality Water quality (Yamuna) Dust pollution 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Focus on pollution and waste management

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

Article Title: 19km roads for end-point connectivity for Hinjewadi Metro
Article Text:
Metro dry runs continue as inauguration awaits

Pune:





The govt is planning to develop a total of 19.2 km of roads for last-mile connectivity for commuters using the upcoming Hinjewadi metro. The roads will be initially developed at eight out of the 12 Metro stations that will be operational in the first leg.The stations include Megapolis circle, Quadron circle, Dohler station, Infosys phase 2 station, Wipro Technologies station, Pall India station, Shivaji Chowk station and Hinjewadi station.Maharashtra Industrial Development Authority (MIDC) and Pune Metropolitan Region Development Authority (PMRDA) will jointly develop the last-mile connectivity roads. The construction work is expected to be completed by Dec. The carriageways will be 12-30 m wide and will have lengths of 0.5-1.5 km. “We have identified residential and office clusters within 500 m of the Metro stations within which these roads will be developed along with footpaths and a bicycle track,” Abhijit Chaudhari, commissioner, PMRDA, said in a meeting held in Sept detailing various proposed works for Hinjewadi IT park.There are four roads proposed at Megapolis circle station with a length of 4.06 km.Roads proposed from this station will be developed by MIDC and gram panchayat. At Quadron circle station, three roads will be built stretching over 3.7 km and developed by MIDC. PMRDA will develop 1.5 km of road starting at Dohler circle station and another 1.1 km road from Wipro Technologies station. MIDC will construct a 500 m road at Infosys phase 2 station. The width of these carriageways will be 18 metres wide.A total of 1.6 km of road will be developed at Pall India station, of which MIDC will build two roads of 400 and 780 metres while PMRDA will develop one road of 400 metres.Shivaji Chowk station, which is expected to be one of the busiest points on the Hinjewadi line, has five last-mile connectivity roads, of which three will be developed by MIDC and two by PMRDA. These five roads will have a total length of 4.9 km connecting with several major areas in the IT park.Lastly, PMRDA will develop three roads starting from Hinjewadi station which will have 1.9-km length in total.
Article Summary: The roads will be initially developed at eight out of the 12 Metro stations that will be operational in the first leg. The carriageways will be 12-30 m wide and will have lengths of 0.5-1.5 km.

Article Title: Mumbai airport crackdown: Afghan, Bangladeshi, Nepalese nationals held with Indian passports
Article Text:
Police said the passports were issued in Mumbai and Kolkata, allegedly with the help of agents. (File Photo)





MUMBAI: Immigration officials at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport intercepted three foreign nationals — from Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Nepal — on October 3 and 4 for allegedly obtaining Indian passports using forged documents and false information.Sahar police said the passports were issued in Mumbai and Kolkata, allegedly with the help of agents. Police are investigating the network involved. All three men were arrested.Bangladeshi national Robindra Mondal, 48, was handed over to police on October 3 after allegedly attempting to travel to Abu Dhabi on an Indian passport. He was scheduled to board Etihad flight EY207 before travelling onward to Paris.Immigration records allegedly linked him to two Bangladeshi passports issued in Dhaka under the name Rabindra Mondol, listing his birthplace as Munshiganj, Bangladesh, and his date of birth as June 12, 1978. Officials said Mondal admitted that he had entered India illegally and later obtained Aadhaar and PAN cards as well as an Indian passport.He allegedly secured Indian passport AP-472113 from Kolkata on May 11, 2026, using false details.Nepalese national Deepak Giri, 40, who arrived from Kathmandu on IndiGo flight 6E1158 on October 3, was questioned after immigration checks showed frequent travel to Kathmandu and he failed to provide satisfactory information.Records showed that Giri was born in Ramechhap, Nepal, held Nepalese citizenship and married a Nepalese citizen in Manthali Municipality on December 14, 2022. His parents had moved to Mumbai in 1980.Police said Giri allegedly obtained an Indian passport from Mumbai on September 16, 2021, using false or incorrect information.Afghan national Taza Khan Zurmati was intercepted on October 4 while allegedly attempting to fly to Dubai as Ibrahim Khan on IndiGo flight 6E-1451. Immigration officials became suspicious after finding Afghan visa stickers in his Indian passport.A biometric search reportedly found two Afghan passports in the names of Taza Khan Zurmati and Taza Khan. Records showed that he entered India on a medical attendant visa on May 19, 2016, returned to Afghanistan on October 15 that year, and re-entered India for treatment on September 5, 2017.Police said Zurmati overstayed after his visa expired and later obtained Aadhaar, PAN and voter ID cards. Using these documents and allegedly false information, he secured Indian passports from the Mumbai Passport Office in 2018 and 2019 under the name Ibrahim Khan.
Article Summary: Immigration officials at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport intercepted three foreign nationals on October 3 and 4. Police said the passports were issued in Mumbai and Kolkata, allegedly with the help of agents. All three men were arrested.

Article Title: Oil prices hover near $100 as Middle East supply holds up, Gulf risks persist
Article Text:
Houthi attacks keep Gulf supply risks alive

Supply squeeze could last

Demand recovery may take longer

Oil prices remained close to $100 a barrel on Tuesday, with steady Middle Eastern oil exports helping to ease supply concerns. However, continued attacks in the region kept traders alert to the risk of disruptions to Gulf supplies.Brent crude was trading at $100.6 a barrel, up 24 cents or 0.24%, while WTI stood at $89.60, gaining 17 cents or 0.19%.The benchmarks have eased from around $103 a barrel after shipping data showed Middle Eastern crude exports had exceeded pre-war levels on four days in the final week of September. Oil shipments held up despite attacks on vessels travelling through the Strait of Hormuz.The supply picture also improved after G7 countries agreed to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude from emergency reserves. The group also pledged not to restrict energy exports following pressure from US President Donald Trump.But the stronger oil flows have not removed concerns about future supplies, with fresh attacks adding to uncertainty over Gulf shipments.Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis said on Monday that they had attacked several sites in Saudi Arabia, including King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, an Aramco refinery in Rabigh and Abha airport.Saudi Arabia had not immediately confirmed the attacks.The attacks came as US-Iran talks remained at a stalemate, while the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Houthi forces continued to raise concerns about possible disruptions to supplies from Saudi Arabia, the region's largest oil exporter."Without a clear diplomatic breakthrough or a further material improvement in export efficiency, the floor under prices looks reasonably firm," Waterer said.The concerns around supply could persist well beyond the immediate crisis. Oil industry executives at a conference in London on Monday said shipping bottlenecks, deep cuts in refinery output and inventory withdrawals that could take years to replace could keep global oil prices high beyond this year.The Strait of Hormuz has been a major source of disruption since the start of the US-Israeli war on Iran at the end of February, when Iran effectively closed the waterway and choked exports through the crucial shipping route.The disruption has been compounded by attacks on oil and gas infrastructure, which have hampered production and affected exports of crude oil and refined fuels."I think it is going to be bedlam for the bulk of the end of the year and maybe 2027," Petronas CEO Tengku Muhammad Taufik said.Saudi Aramco chief executive Amin Nasser said it could take up to two years to rebuild global oil stockpiles that have been drawn down as an emergency measure.Speaking at the Energy Intelligence Forum in London in his first conference address since the start of the Iran war, Nasser said the scale of the stockpile withdrawals would make replenishment a long process."Until Hormuz fully re-opens and confidence returns, the crude reality is that pressure at both ends of the barrel will intensify. Even then, replenishing inventories while meeting demand could take up to two years," he said.Nasser said 3 billion barrels had been lost since the start of the conflict, while 1 billion barrels had been withdrawn from global inventories. The reference to both ends of the barrel covers unrefined crude as well as refined products such as diesel and jet fuel.The supply disruption could also affect the timeline for a recovery in global oil demand.ConocoPhillips Executive Chair Ryan Lance said demand could take until 2028 or 2029 to recover from this year's decline, although he expects it to grow after that.Lance said the floor for US benchmark WTI crude would rise to around $70 a barrel, with a mid-cycle price of $65 to $70 a barrel.US oil production could exceed 14 million to 14.5 million barrels per day if prices remain strong, he said, although he did not specify what he meant by strong prices.Brent futures had traded just above $100 a barrel on Monday, while WTI was close to $90, keeping both benchmarks elevated as traders balanced stronger Middle Eastern exports against the continuing risk of supply disruptions.
Article Summary: Brent crude was trading at $100.6 a barrel, up 24 cents or 0.24%, while WTI stood at $89.60. The benchmarks have eased from around $103 a barrel after shipping data showed Middle Eastern crude exports had exceeded pre-war levels on four days in the final week of September.

Article Title: First India-born cheetahs with Botswana lineage: Kuno welcomes 5 cubs, India's total count now 60
Article Text:
Five cubs were born at Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh, increasing India's cheetah population to 60.





BHOPAL: Project Cheetah crossed another milestone on Sunday with the birth of five cubs at MP's Kuno National Park, taking India's total cheetah count to 60, including 41 born in the country.The cubs were born to 32-month-old cheetah KJ, making her the third India-born female to give birth in the country after Mukhi and KGP12, Union environment minister Bhupender Yadav announced in a social media post, describing it as "an important milestone in the emergence of the next generation of India's cheetah population".The development is an important marker in the progress of Project Cheetah, which aims not only to establish a viable population of the feline in India 70 years after it was declared extinct, but also to enable the species to breed and sustain itself over successive generations, say officials.The birth has an added genetic significance. The father of the five cubs is a male brought from Botswana, making them the first India-born cheetahs to carry the Botswanan lineage. This adds a new genetic lineage to the growing cheetah population in the country.The latest births also reveal a shift in Project Cheetah from the initial phase of relocation from Africa to India to establishing a self-sustaining population through breeding on Indian soil, say officials.Both Yadav and MP chief minister Mohan Yadav congratulated the veterinarians, forest officials, field staff, park management and others associated with Project Cheetah.KJ and her litter will be closely monitored in the coming days, officials said, adding that the initial period is considered critical for newborn cheetahs because cub mortality can be high in the wild.Another generation born on Indian soil adds another chapter to the country's cheetah reintroduction programme, which began with the arrival of the first batch of cheetahs from Namibia in Sept 2022 and subsequently from South Africa.
Article Summary: Five cubs born at Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh, increasing India's cheetah population to 60. Father of the five cubs is a male brought from Botswana, making them the first India-born cheetahs to carry the Botswanan lineage.

Article Title: Ghee, refined oil in her bag: Woman ‘caught stealing’ at Noida DLF Mall, video emerges
Article Text:
At DLF Mall of India in Noida, security apprehended a woman during a bag inspection





NOIDA: A video showing a woman being escorted out of a store at DLF Mall of India in Sector 18 after she was allegedly accused of stealing ghee and refined cooking oil has gone viral on social media. Police and the mall management, however, have not confirmed that the woman stole any items and said she had paid for the products.The video, which is around 30 seconds long, shows two female security guards stopping a woman inside the store and taking her away. The woman can be seen covering her face as she walks out of the premises. During the incident, a store employee can be heard accusing her of stealing goods.Several claims accompanying the video on social media allege that the woman had been visiting the store for around a month and had allegedly taken ghee and refined oil on multiple occasions without paying. Some posts also claim that her activities had been captured on the store’s CCTV cameras.However, no CCTV footage supporting these allegations has been shared along with the viral video. The video itself also does not show the woman stealing any item or leaving the store without making a payment.Following the circulation of the video, information was sought from Sector 20 police. Police said their preliminary inquiry found that the woman had paid for the items she had taken from the store.The mall management also conveyed the same information to the police, officials said.“The woman had paid for the items. The allegations being made on social media have not been established,” police said.The video has triggered a range of reactions on social media, with several users sharing and commenting on the incident. It has reportedly been shared by more than 100 people.Police said the footage currently establishes only that the woman was stopped by security personnel and that a store employee accused her of theft. The circumstances in which the woman was stopped and what transpired inside the store cannot be conclusively determined from the viral video alone.Officials said claims made on social media should not be treated as established facts unless supported by evidence. Police also said that neither the mall nor the store management has submitted a formal complaint regarding theft in connection with the incident so far.Police are examining the available information and other aspects of the incident. Further details will be established if additional evidence, including CCTV footage or statements from those involved, becomes available.
Article Summary: A video showing a woman being escorted out of a store at DLF Mall of India in Noida has gone viral on social media. The video shows two female security guards stopping a woman inside the store and taking her away. During the incident, a store employee can be heard accusing her of stealing goods.

Article Title: Delhi-NCR traffic alert: Central Delhi barricaded amid INDIA bloc march, VIP movement; avoid these routes
Article Text:
Commuters on the Delhi-Noida corridor near Crowne Plaza in Mayur Vihar also reported heavy congestion. (Photo credit: X)

Connaught Place, Old Delhi see heavy congestion

Delhi-Noida corridor also hit

VIP movements add to Delhi's recurring traffic problem

Why is traffic restricted today?





NEW DELHI: Traffic snarls hit several parts of Delhi-NCR on Tuesday as restrictions for the INDIA bloc's march to the Election Commission added to congestion in central Delhi, while commuters on other key stretches reported heavy traffic and prolonged delays.The INDIA bloc MPs marched from the Parliament House complex towards the Election Commission headquarters to demand the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The Delhi Traffic Police had put special arrangements in place from 8am, regulating or diverting traffic around Connaught Place, Patel Chowk, Parliament Street, Jantar Mantar Road, Ashoka Road and adjoining stretches.Commuters were advised to avoid unnecessary travel through the affected areas and expect barricading, diversions and congestion.Heavy traffic was also reported on the Ring Road near AIIMS-Safdarjung Hospital, in and around Connaught Place, on Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Marg in Old Delhi and on the Delhi-Noida corridor near Crowne Plaza, Mayur Vihar.The traffic police separately responded to complaints of prolonged congestion in and around Connaught Place, saying personnel had been deployed at critical junctions and were carrying out active traffic regulation and decongestion measures.On Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Marg in Old Delhi, the traffic police said movement was slow because of prevailing traffic arrangements and high traffic volume. Personnel were deployed at key points to regulate traffic and ease the congestion.On Ring Road near AIIMS-Safdarjung Hospital, the traffic police said it had alerted the concerned traffic circle for immediate deployment and active regulation at critical junctions, merging points and bottlenecks.It also said special attention was being given to ensuring the unhindered movement of ambulances and emergency vehicles.Commuters on the Delhi-Noida corridor near Crowne Plaza in Mayur Vihar also reported heavy congestion.Responding to a commuter's complaint on X, the Delhi Traffic Police said personnel were actively regulating movement and had been deployed at critical merging points and bottlenecks to ensure smoother traffic flow.The traffic police also responded to complaints about congestion around Krishna Menon Marg, Kartavya Path and adjoining roads, saying restrictions were being imposed only when required for operational or security reasons and for the minimum possible duration.The traffic disruption comes a day after the movement of Swiss President Guy Parmelin to Rajghat led to road restrictions and lengthy delays for commuters in central Delhi.During Parmelin's Rajghat visit on Monday, commuters reported being stuck for extended periods around ITO and other key stretches.A recent VIP movement involving Russian President Vladimir Putin had, however, shown that traffic could keep moving despite security restrictions, with congestion clearing relatively quickly.The issue has raised questions over whether better advance planning, deployment and communication can reduce the impact of such movements on daily commuters.The immediate trigger in central Delhi was the INDIA bloc's march to the Election Commission over the SIR exercise. The opposition has accused the poll panel of irregularities in the revision of electoral rolls and has been demanding Kumar's resignation.The protest came a day after the Supreme Court refused to pass an interim order suspending Kumar, while issuing notices to the Centre, the Election Commission and Kumar over allegations concerning decision-making during the SIR process.The court said it would examine whether statutory requirements had been followed.The INDIA bloc's wider campaign includes further protests and programmes against the SIR exercise.For commuters, however, the immediate concern remained the same: long diversions, slow-moving traffic and delays across some of the city's busiest roads.
Article Summary: Heavy traffic reported on Ring Road near AIIMS-Safdarjung Hospital, in and around Connaught Place, on Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Marg in Old Delhi. Commuters on the Delhi-Noida corridor near Crowne Plaza in Mayur Vihar also reported heavy congestion. Traffic disruption comes a day after the movement of Swiss President Guy Parmelin to Rajghat led to road restrictions.

Article Title: Video: Staffer washes utensils in toilet at Korba sweet shop; food dept issues notice
Article Text:
A video showing utensils being washed on a toilet floor at New Delhi Sweets raised significant concerns





RAIPUR: A video showing utensils being washed on a toilet floor at New Delhi Sweets in Korba’s Niharika area has prompted a food safety inspection and an improvement notice, with officials warning of licence suspension if hygiene deficiencies are not addressed within three days.The footage, recorded by a customer and circulated on social media, showed employees washing utensils inside the toilet.Food safety officer Sangharsh Kumar Mishra inspected the outlet following the video’s circulation.During the inspection, the operator attributed the practice to a disruption in water supply, claiming utensils were washed there as an emergency measure.Mishra described the practice as unhygienic and a violation of food safety norms. The establishment was directed to improve its arrangements within two to three days or face suspension of its food licence.
Article Summary: Video shows utensils being washed on a toilet floor at New Delhi Sweets. Food safety officer Sangharsh Kumar Mishra inspected the outlet following the video’s circulation. The operator attributed the practice to a disruption in water supply. Officials warned of licence suspension if hygiene deficiencies are not addressed.

Article Title: 2 workers injured, 500 evacuated after massive fire guts labour camp outside Lucknow airport; watch
Article Text:
Fire broke out at an impermanent housing facility near Chaudhary Charan Singh International Airport in Lucknow
