Improving safety protocols Providing better worker support and compensation Investigating the cause thoroughly Raising awareness among workers 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





LUCKNOW: At least two workers were injured while evacuating a three-storey makeshift labour camp after a major fire engulfed the structure outside Chaudhary Charan Singh International Airport on Tuesday morning.The blaze broke out around 6.50am at the Tata Projects labour colony, about 800 metres from the airport. The PVC-panel structure housed workers engaged in ongoing airport development projects. Thick smoke and flames were visible from several kilometres away, triggering panic in the area.The injured workers were identified as Nirmal, 30, son of Mukhiya, a resident of Saharsa in Bihar, and Rahul Kumar, 26, son of Bhagwati Din Pal, a resident of Salipur in Pratapgarh. Both were taken for medical attention. The Fire Department said neither had sustained burn injuries.The camp had 33 rooms, with 11 on each floor, and could accommodate around 500 workers deployed in round-the-clock shifts. The fire spread rapidly through the combustible panels and engulfed the structure within minutes. Officials did not specify how many workers were present when the fire broke out.The Airport Rescue and Fire Fighting team immediately dispatched a Domestic Fire Tender to the site, while a Crash Fire Tender from the airport and fire tenders from the Uttar Pradesh Fire Service were also deployed.All workers were evacuated safely, officials said.A newly introduced 22,000-litre water bowser was among the fire tenders deployed by the UP Fire Service headquarters. Firefighters climbed to the first and second floors to tackle the flames from close quarters. Two LPG cylinders exploded during the operation, increasing the risk to the firefighting teams.The blaze was brought under control in about 45 minutes and was prevented from spreading to nearby areas. Chief Fire Officer Ankush Mittal reached the site and supervised the operation.An inspection later indicated that the fire started in Barrack 9 while food was being prepared. The temporary structure was completely damaged.“Initial findings shared by Tata Projects indicate that the fire started while some labourers were preparing food using LPG cylinders. The company provides meals for its workers, and the use of flammable materials or unauthorised cooking arrangements within the labour colony is prohibited. Workers had been repeatedly instructed to follow these safety guidelines," said an official source.Following the incident, Tata Projects shifted all affected workers to newly arranged barracks and shelters as a precautionary measure.
Article Summary: Blaze broke out around 6.50am at the Tata Projects labour colony. The PVC-panel structure housed workers engaged in ongoing airport development projects. The injured workers were identified as Nirmal, 30, and Rahul Kumar, 26. Both were taken for medical attention.

Article Title: Bombay HC to X: Remove video against Serum Institute, Adar Poonawalla
Article Text:
Bombay High Court has directed X Corp to take down a recent video uploaded by Yohan Tengra.





MUMBAI: Bombay High Court has directed X Corp to remove a video against Serum Institute of India Pvt Ltd and its CEO Adar Poonawalla that was uploaded by a social media influencer Yohan Tengra immediately after its June 5, 2023 order.Justice Gauri Godse of HC on Tuesday passed the order on SII and Poonawalla’s interim application in the pending defamation suit regarding content posted against the company and its COVID-19 vaccine. She also issued show-cause notices to Tengra, his organisation Anarchy for Freedom India, Ambar Koiri and TV 10 L.I.V.E, an online news portal, as to why action should not be taken for defying HC’s order. The notices are returnable on Oct 27.The application said Tengra and four defendants were restrained by the June 5, 2023 order from publishing or circulating defamatory videos and content. The same night Tengra uploaded a fresh video. On June 9, 2023, the plaintiffs issued a takedown notice to Google and X. Google complied but X refused, stating HC’s order was not issued against it.Advocate Karl Tamboly, for SII and Poonawalla, said videos uploaded were held to be unlawful by the June 5, 2023 order.Hence, videos and content of a like nature are also directed to be removed. He said in the absence of Tengra complying with HC’s direction, X is obligated to remove the objectionable content. Advocate Mayur Khandeparkar, for X, said the plaintiffs must initiate contempt proceedings against the defendants instead of waging a proxy battle with an intermediary.Justice Godse said it is undisputed that the objectionable content is still available with X. Tengra uploaded the fresh video not only in blatant defiance of HC’s injunction order “but he also states that he will not comply with the directions of the court and that he would not stop calling plaintiff no. 2 (Poonawalla) ‘a mass murderer’.”The judge noted there were no directions to X to remove the objectionable content and, thus, it cannot be held liable for the objectionable content not removed by the five defendants or for the new content uploaded by Tengra. Citing a Supreme Court judgment, she said even if an intermediary is exempt from liability for third-party information, necessary directions can be issued to remove the unlawful or prohibited content.Considering the “subsequent circumstance” of Tengra uploading the fresh video, Justice Godse said sufficient grounds are made out to direct X to “remove, delete or disable access” to the fresh video uploaded by Tengra.
Article Summary: Bombay High Court has directed X Corp to remove a video against Serum Institute of India Pvt Ltd and its CEO Adar Poonawalla. The video was uploaded by social media influencer Yohan Tengra immediately after its June 5, 2023 order.

Article Title: India's factory growth hits 7 month high in September, thanks to demand and hiring boost
Article Text:
Factory growth hits 7-month high, PMI rises to 55.1

India’s manufacturing activity scaled up sharply in September, as stronger demand pushed up sales and production, while companies stepped up hiring and stock-building.The seasonally adjusted HSBC India Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rose to 55.1 in September, from 52.8 in August, marking the strongest improvement in the sector’s health in seven months. A PMI reading above 50 indicates expansion, while a reading below 50 signals contraction.The recovery in factory activity was supported by both domestic and overseas demand. Stronger new orders helped drive production higher, with demand across electronics, food, pharma and textiles taking total sales growth to its highest level since February.Export orders also gained momentum during the month, with manufacturers reporting increased business from clients in Brazil, Europe, the UAE and the US."India's factory sector ended the quarter on a firmer footing. The PMI rose to 55.1 in September, up from 52.8, as stronger domestic and overseas demand lifted sales and production. Hiring resumed at its fastest pace since May, and manufacturers became more optimistic about the months ahead," Pranjul Bhandari, chief India economist at HSBC, told PTI.The improvement in demand was accompanied by a renewed increase in factory employment.After a blip in August, job growth resumed in September, with the pace of employment expansion described by panellists as solid and the strongest since May.Manufacturers also became more confident about the months ahead. Output forecasts were upgraded during September, taking overall positive sentiment to a four-month high. The outlook was supported by a healthy pipeline of new enquiries and expectations that strong demand would continue.The expectation of higher future sales also prompted companies to increase their purchases of materials and build inventories. Overall buying activity expanded at a faster pace than in August."Companies bought more materials and built up stocks to prepare for anticipated sales. Finished goods inventories recorded their second-largest increase in nearly 12 years, signalling a clear shift from leaner stock levels," Bhandari said.Finished goods inventories rose for the third consecutive month. The increase was the second-fastest in 11-and-a-half years, behind July, as manufacturers actively accumulated stocks in anticipation of stronger demand.At the same time, companies faced quicker increases in input costs and selling prices. Despite the acceleration, the rates of inflation remained mild by historical standards.The September reading came as manufacturing activity regained momentum after the slower expansion recorded in August, with the PMI rising by more than two points during the month."Holdings of finished products increased for the third month in a row and at the second-fastest pace in 11-and-a-half years (behind July)," the report said.The HSBC India Manufacturing PMI is compiled by S&P Global based on responses from purchasing managers at around 400 manufacturers.
Article Summary: HSBC India Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rose to 55.1 in September, from 52.8 in August. Stronger new orders helped drive production higher, with demand across electronics, food, pharma and textiles taking total sales growth to its highest level since February.

Article Title: Anthropic targets $2 trillion valuation despite huge spending and billions in losses
Article Text:
Anthropic targets $2 trillion valuation despite huge spending and billions in losses

Revenue growth draws investor attention

Huge infrastructure spending

Losses add to valuation questions

Customer concentration remains a risk

Anthropic has put a massive price tag on the AI boom, backing it with an equally heavy spending plan.The AI giant is heading towards a potential valuation of more than $2 trillion even as it plans $518 billion in cloud computing and infrastructure obligations in the coming years.The company’s IPO prospectus, seen by Reuters, also shows just how quickly its business has grown. Anthropic’s revenue reportedly rose 12-fold in 2025, giving investors a strong growth story to weigh against its continuing losses and huge infrastructure commitments.The scale of its plans has also spilled into markets, with European technology shares rising 2.4% and the US chip index gaining 1.5%.For investors, Anthropic’s rapid expansion is a key part of the valuation story.Michael Field, chief equity strategist at Morningstar, Amsterdam, said the speed of the company’s growth stood out in the prospectus."If anything, the acceleration of the business is the biggest part of this release. Growing a big business can be difficult, but the prospectus stating that revenue grew by 12 fold in 2025 is truly remarkable."Field said the proposed valuation should be considered alongside the company’s sales."Obviously a $2 trillion valuation sounds outlandish, but when you break it down to a multiple of sales, likely to be around 18-20x, it sounds much more reasonable than the recent SpaceX IPO."Anthropic’s plans also show that the AI investment cycle is continuing to require substantial spending on infrastructure.Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB Platform, London, said the planned spending was positive for companies involved in semiconductors and AI infrastructure."This is positive for the AI trade, since it is fuelled by continued elevated levels of capex spend. The fact that Anthropic is planning on spending big on capex means that the capex cycle is not over yet. This is good news for semiconductor and AI infrastructure companies. I believe that if Anthropic had signalled a lower level of spending, this could have caused a wobble in the AI trade, since it would lead to fears about the sustainability of the AI trade as we move into Q4. "The prospectus puts rapid revenue growth alongside the large infrastructure commitments needed to support it.Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club, London, said Anthropic’s expectations for AI’s economic impact appeared to have supported demand for European technology stocks."It's the vision and the projections to the extent to which Anthropic believes AI will be a game changer for economies around the world that seem to have lifted demand for European tech stocks."She also raised concerns over the company’s spending while it remains loss-making."There still will be niggles of concern among some about the huge sums that are projected to be spent even though it is making a loss. But that hasn't caused a flutter of general fear because, overall, there still seems to be a pretty hefty appetite for AI focused investments."Anthropic’s losses remain another factor in the debate around its proposed valuation.Field said the losses were a concern when considered against the company’s current revenue, growth rate and size. However, he said investors had already absorbed much of the spending story."The losses certainly are a concern. Particularly given the growth rate and the size relative to current revenues. It's unlikely to deter investors, however, with the spend story having been digested for some time now."He said the scale of planned investment also reflected management’s confidence in future demand."The key takeaway for investors is the confidence in the business and the AI strategy. Yes spend is high and growing, but management obviously feel the growth rate inherent in demand is sufficiently attractive to keep spending, hence why they are coming to market and demanding a top-dollar valuation."Anthropic’s revenue growth is another area attracting attention, particularly because a significant share reportedly comes from a small number of customers.Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell, London, said the company’s revenue growth had become the main focus despite its spending plans. "Massive spending would normally have investors running for the hills, but what's capturing the market's attention is Anthropic's stellar revenue growth, up 12-fold in 2025. Admittedly, AI is moving at such a rapid pace that last year’s sales achievements relate to technology that is already outdated. "Anthropic’s IPO plans therefore bring together rapid revenue growth, continuing losses and a huge infrastructure commitment. The company is seeking a valuation of more than $2 trillion while planning $518 billion in cloud computing and infrastructure obligations.
Article Summary: Anthropic is heading towards a potential valuation of more than $2 trillion. It plans $518 billion in cloud computing and infrastructure obligations in the coming years. Anthropic’s revenue reportedly rose 12-fold in 2025, giving investors a strong growth story to weigh against its continuing losses.

Article Title: RBI rate hikes ahead? BofA sees 100 bps repo rate increase through H1 2027
Article Text:
BofA sees 100 bps repo rate increase through H1 2027

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) could raise interest rates by 100 basis points through the first half of 2027, according to Bank of America (BofA) Securities. The brokerage has also moved up its estimate for the first rate hike, now expecting the hike in October instead of December.BofA expects the RBI to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points at its October 7 monetary policy meeting, and then another 75 basis points of hikes, taking the projected terminal rate to 6.25 per cent.The new forecast is twice the size of BofA's earlier 50 basis point estimate.“Our bigger forecast shift is arguably the quantum of hikes, as we are raising our total quantum of hikes from 50bp earlier, to 100bp now,” BofA said.BofA expects the RBI to raise rates by 50 basis points in the fourth quarter of 2026 and another 50 basis points in the first half of 2027. It also expects the central bank to change its monetary policy stance in December.“The RBI will switch the stance in December to one of calibrated tightening”, the report said.So, what has changed in BofA's view? The brokerage said the domestic economy remains resilient, giving the RBI less reason to wait before raising rates.At the same time, inflation risks are becoming broader.Oil prices remained around $100-110 per barrel for most of September, BofA said. It also pointed to rising risks of fuel price increases and food-related supply pressures.Strong economic growth is another factor behind the revised outlook. BofA said the strength of the economy is reducing the need for the RBI to keep monetary conditions accommodative.Non-food credit growth stood at 17.8 per cent year-on-year in September, while investment demand is expected to remain healthy in the second quarter of FY27.Inflation pressures are also spreading, according to the report. BofA said food inflation is becoming more broad-based, while wholesale inflation is increasingly spreading to other sectors. Tradables inflation rose to 5.9 per cent in August 2026.The brokerage has also laid out a scenario in which the RBI could go beyond the 100-basis-point increase it currently expects. If real GDP growth stays around 7 per cent and headline inflation remains close to 5.5 per cent, BofA said the central bank could raise rates by more than 100 basis points.In that case, front-end rates could rise above 6.5 per cent, the brokerage said.But a sharp slowdown in growth could change the rate outlook. BofA said the RBI could deliver fewer hikes or no hike if growth falls below 7 per cent and moves towards 6 per cent on a forward-looking basis.
Article Summary: Bank of America Securities sees 100 bps repo rate increase through H1 2027. BofA expects the RBI to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points at its October 7 monetary policy meeting, and then another 75 basis points of hikes, taking the projected terminal rate to 6.25 per cent.

Article Title: 90% of dementia cases in TN go undiagnosed: State turns focus to early screening and care
Article Text:
About 35% of those screened had hypertension, which, says Ramani, is among the risk factors for dementia (AI Image)





CHENNAI: With more than five lakh people in Tamil Nadu living with dementia, and 90% believed to be undiagnosed, the state is looking at making the condition a “public health priority”.“Tamil Nadu has a rapidly ageing population. People over 60 make up 16% of the population in 2026, and it is projected to reach 20% in 10 years. The number of people with dementia is projected to double to 10 lakh,” says Ramani Sundaram of Dementia India Alliance (DIA), which recently organised DemCon in Chennai, a conference on the condition.DIA is a national organisation focused on dementia awareness, care, support and brain healthAt DemCon, state health minister K G Arunraj said the govt would work towards a “coordinated state plan”. “The MoU between the department of health and family welfare and DIA is an important step in this direction,” said Arun Raj. “This partnership is an expression of our shared commitment to strengthening dementia care.”The state plan will look at standardising screening, assessment, referral and treatment, as well as making diagnosis, systematic referrals and follow-up part of the existing primary healthcare infrastructure.“It’s important to create awareness as dementia care costs about Rs 3 lakh per person annually, apart from the informal cost of care provided by family members,” says Ramani. “Cognitive impairment cannot be reduced to simply asking an elderly person whether they are becoming forgetful. ”An ongoing screening programme conducted since Feb by DIA in collaboration with the state govt among 2,500 elderly people in Coimbatore, Erode and Chengalpet, found 9% had cognitive impairment.Among those screened, 30% reported neurological problems such as slowness, tremors, falls or limb weakness, while 28% had sleep disturbances. About 27% reported feeling sad, irritable, or disinterested in their usual activities, while 18% had trouble with memory, wayfinding or planning. About 12% had difficulty speaking, understanding, naming, reading or writing, and 7% said they heard voices or saw images when alone.About 35% of those screened had hypertension, which, says Ramani, is among the risk factors for dementia. “There was substance abuse in about 15% of those screened, while a large percentage – 42 – chewed tobacco. These are also among the risk factors. Up to 45% of dementia can be prevented if these are addressed. So, this is an important part of the action plan to make Tamil Nadu a dementia-aware state,” says Ramani.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu has a rapidly ageing population. People over 60 make up 16% of the population in 2026, and it is projected to reach 20% in 10 years. More than five lakh people in Tamil Nadu living with dementia, and 90% believed to be undiagnosed. The state is looking at making the condition a ‘public health priority’

Article Title: As Elon Musk plans to shake up mobile industry, AT&T CEO John Stankey says that the economics and technical aspects of Starlink's plan don't line up
Article Text:
Starlink aims to challenge telecom operators

AT&T's counter-bet: fiber over satellite

Starlink's mobile ambitions

The cost problem

Why Stankey says the math doesn't work

Analysts remain skeptical too

AT&T CEO John Stankey has cast doubt on Musk's plans to turn SpaceX's Starlink satellite network into a direct competitor to wireless carriers, arguing that the economics and technical realities behind the strategy do not add up. Speaking to Axios, Stankey described SpaceX's ambition of becoming a major challenger to traditional telecom companies as "not a viable strategy," even as Elon Musk and Gwynne Shotwell, president of SpaceX, have outlined plans to expand Starlink beyond satellite internet and into mobile services.The comments come as SpaceX seeks to leverage Starlink's growing satellite network to compete more directly with established telecom operators. Shotwell recently said she expects Starlink to win customers from traditional carriers, arguing that the company's service would be superior. The remarks rattled investors, with shares of major telecom firms including AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile reportedly falling after SpaceX highlighted its ambitions. According to SpaceX's public disclosures, Starlink had 12 million subscribers and a constellation of 10,200 satellites covering 167 countries as of June 30.The connectivity business accounted for 55% of SpaceX's revenue, making it the company's biggest revenue generator.AT&T is leaning hard on fiber infrastructure to grow its internet business at a moment when AI is driving surging demand for connectivity. The company announced a $3 billion deal with Corning on Tuesday to expand that infrastructure, arguing fiber delivers speeds three times faster than satellite. Stankey was blunt about the comparison, telling Axios that nothing beats fiber, and that even if satellite technology performs at its absolute best over the next decade, it still won't be able to match what fiber delivers.Starlink already competes with traditional telecom companies for home and business internet customers, and SpaceX has now started talking openly about a mobile business that would put it in direct competition with wireless carriers. Shotwell added fuel to that narrative in August, during SpaceX's first earnings call as a public company, predicting the company would win over a meaningful number of customers because its service would simply be better. That comment sent shares of AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile falling the following day.As of June 30, Starlink had 12 million subscribers and more than 10,200 satellites providing coverage across 167 countries. While SpaceX's rockets and AI work tend to dominate headlines, its connectivity business is actually its largest revenue driver, accounting for 55% of total sales.Becoming a genuine fourth major US mobile carrier would require significantly more terrestrial infrastructure to match a traditional cellular network's capacity — a build-out one analyst estimated could cost SpaceX more than $100 billion. SpaceX's alternative: installing small cellular base stations alongside Starlink dishes at homes and businesses, adding ground-based capacity where satellite alone falls short, without building a sprawling cell tower network. Musk claims these stations could eventually deliver connectivity directly to phones with better and higher bandwidth than existing carriers offer.Stankey argued that installing enough small stations to match a traditional network's capacity would cost roughly the same as building a full macro cellular network. He also flagged a regulatory hurdle: current law doesn't allow radiating cellular signals from someone's home without their permission, unless the law changes. If the approach were genuinely viable, he argued, AT&T would already be doing it on its own fiber network. SpaceX did not respond to a request for comment.Bernstein analyst Madison Rezaei wrote that cell towers aren't going anywhere soon, even if Musk gets creative, citing technical hurdles extending satellite coverage indoors, limited brand awareness, and customer reluctance to switch carriers. She suggested Starlink Mobile could fill a meaningful gap in remote, rural, maritime, or disaster scenarios, but remains a long way from replacing terrestrial carrier networks. operators' brands. She said Starlink Mobile could prove valuable in rural, remote, maritime and disaster-response scenarios but remains "a long way" from replacing terrestrial cellular networks.Despite the scepticism, the growing confrontation between SpaceX and established telecom providers highlights how satellite-based connectivity is increasingly moving into territory historically dominated by mobile network operators. As both sides invest billions to shape the future of communications, the battle between fibre, cellular networks and satellite internet appears set to intensify.
Article Summary: AT&T CEO John Stankey casts doubt on SpaceX's plans to become a direct competitor to wireless carriers. Stankey argued that installing enough small stations to match a traditional network's capacity would cost roughly the same as building a full macro cellular network. The comments come as SpaceX seeks to leverage Starlink's growing satellite network to compete more directly with established telecom operators.

Article Title: Amazon Web Services' Swami Sivasubramanian says that CEOs are no longer worried if AI will add value to their businesses, now they have a new 'fear'
Article Text:
AI has boosted profits, but the jump is not substantial

The ‘Big AI Question’ seems to have changed. Until 2025, the general artificial intelligence (AI) worry was if investment in the technology was really worth it and if it will add to the bottomline. The same has shifted in 2026, and now the key concern is how safe are AI Agents. Companies do not yet trust AI with important decisions. According to a report by GeekWire, this was the general consensus at the recent Madrona's IA40 Summit. The Madrona's IA40 Summit is the venture capital company's annual gathering of AI startups, investors and tech executives. Zico Kolter, the Carnegie Mellon professor who chairs the safety and security committee of OpenAI's board, said that as of now Companies do not yet trust AI with important decisions. According to Kolter, the ability to control AI systems has to keep pace with their capabilities, which might mean developing them more slowly than is possible.His view was shared by Amazon Web Services (AWS) Agentic AI and Emerging Technologies organization head Swami Sivasubramanian. AWS's top executives said that most CEOs and CTOs worry about whether an AI agent will always follow their company’s rules and regulations.Speaking at the Summit, Sivasubramanian said that nearly every CIO and CEO raises the same question about AI agents. “How do I know it is always going to obey all my rules and regulations?” he said. “This is a real concern.” He added that companies can keep the creativity of AI models by pairing them with separate systems that check a model’s work against the company’s rules and catch violations.Sivasubramanian said that one of the least appreciated parts of making AI agents work is getting them the right company data for the task. He pointed out that teams inside Amazon were showing him impressive AI agents they had built in two or three weeks. When he asked when the agents could be rolled out, he said that almost every team told him it still had to work out security, identity and monitoring.AWS in June announced a service for that purpose, called AWS Context, which maps the relationships in a company’s data for agents to use. Sivasubramanian said it’s meant to work across platforms and cloud providers, and he expects this kind of service to be a basic building block for the next 20 years, as cloud storage and databases were two decades ago.McKinsey senior partner Lari Hamalainen reportedly said that about 40% of companies claim AI has increased their profits, but only 6% describe the increase as substantial. Even as AI becomes more and more capable, there’s still lots of work to do to close the gap between “the goals, the capabilities, and what we all are aspiring to do,” McIlwain said.Madrona’s closing slide at the Summit said that returns on AI are still early for most of the companies using it but look inevitable based on what the earliest adopters are seeing.
Article Summary: Companies do not yet trust AI with important decisions. Amazon's Swami Sivasubramanian said that most CEOs and CTOs worry about whether an AI agent will always follow their company’s rules and regulations. About 40% of companies claim AI has increased their profits, but only 6% describe the increase as substantial.

Article Title: In 2009, Google's Eric Schmidt and wife Wendy bought a former fisheries ship; by 2022, the vessel offered free research access and had mapped over 1.3 million square kilometres of seafloor
Article Text:
Eric Schmidt and Wendy Schmidt donated to Italy's National Research Council

Hosted more than 1,000 scientists

The mission continues with a bigger ship

Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt and Wendy Schmidt transformed a former fisheries protection vessel into a philanthropic ocean research platform that, by 2022, had hosted more than 1,000 scientists and mapped over 1.3 million square kilometres of the ocean floor. According to Schmidt Ocean Institute, the vessel, named Falkor, was originally built in 1981 as a fishery protection ship. It was acquired by the Schmidts in 2009 when they founded the Schmidt Ocean Institute, an organisation focused on advancing oceanographic research and exploration. After undergoing an extensive two-year refit, Falkor was converted into what the institute described as the world's first year-round philanthropic research vessel made available to scientists at no cost.Rather than retiring the vessel, Schmidt Ocean Institute donated Falkor to Italy's Consiglio Nazionale delle Ricerche (CNR), the country's largest research organization, comprising 88 institutes nationwide and a marine science community of more than 450 researchers. Under CNR, the ship was renamed Gaia Blu and continues operating in the Mediterranean and beyond.Wendy Schmidt, co-founder of Schmidt Ocean Institute, said that after a decade of remarkable discoveries and scientific research, she and Eric couldn't imagine a better home for Falkor than CNR, expressing confidence that the agency would continue the ship's legacy of ocean exploration, supporting marine science, and bringing the wonders of the ocean to the public.Eric Schmidt echoed that sentiment, pointing to CNR's century of scientific experience and its track record of investing in talented researchers as reasons he believed the organization was an excellent new home for the vessel, adding that he looked forward to seeing what further discoveries would emerge from Falkor's continued work at sea.CNR president Prof. Maria Chiara Carrozza called the donation extremely beneficial for both CNR and the wider Italian scientific community, noting that it would help foster collaboration with international research institutes and universities studying the Mediterranean basin — one of the cradles of human civilization, and a region heavily impacted by human activity. She added that the vessel would give Italian scientists a unique opportunity to pursue multi-year ocean research as part of both European and other international projects.According to the institute, Falkor completed 81 research expeditions and hosted 1,056 international scientists during its time in service. The ship travelled a distance equivalent to more than 12 trips around the world while supporting marine research projects across multiple oceans.The vessel's explorations contributed to several notable discoveries, including a 500-metre-tall coral reef in Australia's Great Barrier Reef, deep-sea coral "gardens" off Western Australia, and rare footage of the elusive glass octopus.Schmidt Ocean Institute didn't step back from ocean research after donating Falkor — instead, it transitioned to an even larger vessel, Falkor (too), which launched in early fall 2022 after being outfitted with what the organization described as some of the most sophisticated maritime technology available. At 110 metres, the new ship is significantly larger than its predecessor, and has continued the Institute's core mission: operating the world's only year-round philanthropic research vessel made available to the international scientific community entirely free of cost.
Article Summary: Eric and Wendy Schmidt donated a former fisheries protection vessel to Italy's National Research Council. The vessel, named Falkor, hosted more than 1,000 scientists and mapped over 1.3 million square kilometres of the ocean floor. Under CNR, the ship was renamed Gaia Blu and continues operating in the Mediterranean and beyond.

Article Title: Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison bought an 8.4-acre Florida oceanfront estate for $80 million in 2021; five years later, after shelving demolition plans, he is asking $165 million for the property
Article Text:
All about Larry Ellison’s oceanfront property

What the neighborhood market looks like

Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison builds up his holdings in Manalapan

Larry Ellison, the co-founder of Oracle, is resisting his sprawling oceanfront estate in North Palm Beach, Florida for $165 million, more than double the $80 million he paid for the property in 2021, according to a report by the Wall Street Journal. This move from Ellison comes five years after the billionaire purchased the 8.4-acre estate and abandoned the plans to demolish the existing mansion. As per the WSJ report, the new asking price is around 14% higher than the $145 million price which the price at which the property was first listed in 2022. The estate is located within the exclusive Seminole Landing grated community in North Palm Beach. After acquiring the property in 2021, Ellison reportedly considered tearing down the Mediterranean-style mansion but never proceeded with the redevelopment. Instead, the estate remained largely unused while the billionaire focused on expanding other real estate holdings in South Florida.The latest $165 million asking price would set a record for North Palm Beach if achieved, reflecting the growing demand for ultra-luxury waterfront properties in the region.The estate's biggest draw is its land and beachfront access rather than the house itself. The property spans 8.4 acres and has 562 feet of Atlantic frontage, making it the third-largest oceanfront parcel in Palm Beach County.The main house has 16,284 square feet of living space, seven bedrooms, eight full bathrooms and five half-bathrooms. Other features include a swimming pool and spa, a tennis court, a four-car garage, direct beach access and a helipad. At $165 million, the price works out to more than $10,000 per square foot and about $20 million per acre. That would set a record for North Palm Beach.Seminole Landing sits next to the Seminole Golf Club. In 2020, private-equity billionaire Robert F. Smith bought a pair of houses there from energy drinks entrepreneur Russ Weiner for $48.19 million. Sales of $100 million or more have become almost routine in neighboring Palm Beach. Kenny and Kaneb said a market of $50 million and up is starting to take shape in North Palm Beach too. A property there sold for $55 million last year. Ellison's ask is three times that figure.The relisting comes as Ellison builds up his holdings in Manalapan, an affluent town just south of Palm Beach, about 30 miles from the North Palm Beach estate. In June, he paid about $35 million for a parcel next to his roughly 15-acre compound there. He paid $173 million for the original compound in 2022. His Florida holdings also include housing for staff. In 2023, he spent almost $10 million to buy eight homes in a lakefront community in Boynton Beach, about 30 minutes from the Manalapan compound.Ellison's property portfolio also includes homes in Malibu, Calif., and Lake Tahoe, as well as the Hawaiian island of Lanai. He has recently been a major financial backer of Paramount's $81 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, the Journal reported.
Article Summary: The 8.4-acre estate is located in the exclusive Seminole Landing grated community in North Palm Beach. The main house has 16,284 square feet of living space, seven bedrooms, eight full bathrooms and five half-bathrooms. At $165 million, the price works out to more than $10,000 per square foot and about $20 million per acre.

Article Title: ‘Rockstar food inspector': Maharashtra FDA chief Tukaram Mundhe gets New York Times front-page spotlight
Article Text:
Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration chief Tukaram Mundhe is recognized for his rigorous food safety enforcement measures

More than 12,000 food inspections

Using technology to expand enforcement

Crackdown extends beyond restaurants





NEW DELHI: Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration chief Tukaram Mundhe has been dubbed a “rockstar” by The New York Times for his aggressive crackdown on food safety violations, with the American newspaper featuring the IAS officer on its front page and highlighting how his surprise inspections have turned routine regulatory enforcement into a highly visible campaign.The NYT described Mundhe as a “food safety celebrity” and highlighted the contrast between diners who revere him and restaurant owners who fear his inspections. The international attention comes as the Maharashtra FDA steps up action against restaurants, food businesses, pharmacies, warehouses and other establishments across the state.Mundhe, however, sought to shift the focus from the international recognition to the larger purpose of food safety enforcement. Sharing the report on X, he said, “Good governance is not about making headlines. It is about making a difference.”“Food safety is ultimately about protecting people, upholding standards and building public trust,” he said, adding that fair, fearless and consistent enforcement helps strengthen the credibility of institutions.The international recognition comes amid a major enforcement push by the Maharashtra FDA.Between June 1 and August 31, the department conducted 12,083 food inspections and collected 37,604 food and drug samples. It issued 5,269 improvement notices and suspended 603 food licences during the period.The department also seized food stock worth Rs 67.2 crore and reported 875 arrests in food-related cases. On the drug side, it carried out 2,902 inspections and seized illegal medicines and cosmetics worth Rs 11.41 crore.The crackdown also targeted banned gutkha and pan masala. The FDA registered 644 FIRs, made 867 arrests and seized stocks worth Rs 19.62 crore.During a separate festive-season crackdown between September 23 and 27, the department suspended food licences and seized 50,601.78 kg of food stock worth Rs 1.19 crore across several divisions.The FDA is also turning to digital systems and AI to deal with manpower constraints. Its sanctioned strength is 1,271, while a roadmap submitted by the commissioner estimates that nearly three times as many personnel would be required to meet regulatory needs across Maharashtra.Its online system tracks complaints, assigns them to officers and sets response deadlines, with higher authorities alerted when action is delayed. The system also creates an audit trail so senior officials can monitor cases in real time.The department is looking at combining inspection records, laboratory results, complaints, licensing information and previous violations to identify establishments and products requiring greater scrutiny.Mundhe has described AI as a tool to help the existing workforce “see more, respond faster”, rather than replace officers.The FDA's enforcement drive has also extended to pharmacies, with action against the sale of antibiotics without prescriptions and hundreds of pharmacy licences cancelled or suspended. Mundhe has also raised concerns over high margins on hospital consumables and recommended bringing such products under regulated pricing.On the food side, the department has imposed a one-year ban on the manufacture, storage, distribution and transportation of analogue paneer. It is also working on measures to improve food packaging, including a proposal for food-grade, non-toxic ink in newsprint used to wrap street food.The FDA has also brought weddings, community gatherings and other large events under greater food-safety scrutiny, requiring caterers and event operators to comply with registration and safety requirements.Alongside enforcement, the department is pushing awareness among consumers. Under its “Safe Food for Every School Child” initiative, it conducted 270 workshops involving 60,990 schools across Maharashtra between April 1 and September 11.Mundhe's broader strategy is built around three pillars — Empower, Enable and Enforce — with the stated aim of making food and medicine safety a continuing public-health priority rather than something addressed only when violations are detected.
Article Summary: Mahar Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration chief Tukaram Mundhe has been dubbed a ‘rockstar’ by The New York Times. The international attention comes as the Maharashtra FDA steps up action against restaurants, food businesses, pharmacies, warehouses and other establishments.

Article Title: A Ford factory in Mexico was facing pigeon invasions, forcing 4,000 workers to deal with bird poo, then a hawk named El Charro was hired and cut bird activity by 80%
Article Text:
Pigeon invasions at Ford’s Mexico factory

Ford turns to a real predator

El Charro patrols the plant

Bird activity drops by about 80%

From pest control to factory celebrity

Ford’s Hermosillo assembly plant in Sonora, Mexico, found itself dealing with an unusual workplace problem involving persistent pigeons entering the sprawling factory and leaving droppings around equipment and freshly painted vehicles. The facility employs more than 4,000 workers and produces more than 300,000 vehicles a year, making the bird problem difficult to ignore. Ford tried conventional deterrents, including predator sounds and fake predator eyes, but the pigeons gradually became accustomed to them. The company eventually turned to a more natural solution by bringing in a trained Harris’s hawk named El Charro. Since July 2025, the hawk has patrolled the facility for several hours a day, with Ford reporting an approximately 80% decline in bird activity in monitored areas.The pigeon problem at Ford’s Hermosillo plant was more than an occasional nuisance. Birds repeatedly found their way into the facility, while their droppings created hygiene concerns and could end up on vehicles and around machinery. With thousands of employees working across the massive manufacturing complex, keeping the birds away became an ongoing challenge. Ford initially tried methods designed to make the factory appear unsafe for pigeons.These included sounds associated with predatory birds and visual deterrents resembling the eyes of predators. But the pigeons eventually learned that the threats were not real. Their persistence reportedly reached the point where they could wait for factory doors to open before entering.After artificial deterrents failed to solve the problem, Ford turned to falconry. In July 2025, the company brought in El Charro, a trained Harris’s hawk, to patrol the facility. The species, Parabuteo unicinctus, is native to the Americas and is widely used in professional bird-control operations. The purpose of El Charro’s presence is primarily deterrence. His presence signals to pigeons that a genuine predator is nearby, encouraging them to leave the area or avoid settling there in the first place.El Charro typically spends around two to three hours a day patrolling the Ford facility. Before his patrol, he is fed, allowing the operation to focus on controlling bird activity rather than relying on him to hunt pigeons for food. The hawk also helps identify areas where pigeons gather or build nests. Once those locations are identified, workers can remove nests and address places where birds repeatedly congregate. According to Ford, El Charro has completed more than 300 flights and logged more than 1,170 hours of patrol time since he began working at the plant.Ford says the unusual strategy has produced a substantial improvement. Bird activity in the monitored areas has fallen by about 80% since the hawk began patrolling the facility. The figure refers specifically to bird activity in monitored areas and should not be interpreted as an 80% reduction in the overall pigeon population. El Charro’s role is part of a broader bird-control programme that combines predator deterrence with nest removal and other measures. The use of trained birds of prey for bird control is already established in several industries. Airports, landfills, agricultural sites and other large facilities sometimes use falcons or hawks to discourage unwanted birds from gathering in areas where they can cause safety, hygiene or operational problems.El Charro has also become an unusual presence among workers at the Hermosillo plant. Employees have been photographed with the hawk, and Ford has highlighted him as an unconventional member of the factory workforce. His success illustrates the difference between artificial and natural deterrents. Pigeons were able to become accustomed to recorded predator sounds and fake predator images, but the presence of a trained raptor creates a genuine predator threat. For Ford, a persistent pigeon problem at one of its largest manufacturing facilities has therefore produced an unusual solution. Instead of continuing to rely only on fake predators, the company brought in a real one, turning El Charro into one of the factory’s most unconventional workers.
Article Summary: Ford’s Hermosillo assembly plant in Sonora, Mexico, found itself dealing with an unusual workplace problem involving persistent pigeons. The facility employs more than 4,000 workers and produces more than 300,000 vehicles a year. Ford tried conventional deterrents, including predator sounds and fake predator eyes, but the pigeons gradually became accustomed to them. The company eventually turned to a more natural solution by bringing in a trained Harris's hawk named El Charro.

Article Title: How to know if your health insurance coverage is enough for your age
Article Text:
Health insurance needs rarely remain the same throughout life.

By Sarbvir Singh

What determines how much health insurance you need?

1. Age and life stage

2. Where you live

3. Individual cover or family floater?

4. Pre-existing diseases and waiting periods

5. The policy’s actual coverage, not just its sum insured

(The author is Joint Group CEO, PB Fintech)

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

Is having health insurance the same as having enough health insurance? Not always. Some buy in their 20s, while others might realise its importance after a hospitalisation well into their 30s. But one question that looms large for every consumer is - how much health insurance is enough. The answer is - there isn’t a single universal magic number that’s fit for everyone. Just like our life stages, health insurance needs do not remain static for a lifetime.A health insurance policy can be perfectly adequate on the day you buy it and inadequate a few years later. The reason? Our financial lives change faster than our insurance cover often does. What makes the difference is not age alone, but what that person is trying to protect. The mistake is to treat the sum insured as a number that can be chosen once and forgotten. Here’s how health insurance coverage for different stages should ideally look like:Age is a useful starting point, but adequate health cover is determined by a combination of healthcare costs, family circumstances and the terms of the policy itself. Five factors deserve particular attention are -Health insurance needs rarely remain the same throughout life. A young professional may initially need individual cover, but marriage, children and ageing parents can change both the number of people who need protection and the financial exposure involved. In one's 40s, for instance, a hospitalisation may coincide with home loan repayments, children's education expenses and responsibility for parents. As healthcare needs change with age, the existing sum insured should be reviewed rather than assumed to be sufficient simply because it was adequate when first purchased.The same medical procedure can cost very different amounts depending on the city and hospital. If you stay in a metro city like Mumbai, Delhi or Bangalore, the treatment cost will be inclusive of higher room rent, consultation fee, procedure and medicine costs as compared to a Tier 2 city. This does not mean everyone living in a metro city needs the highest available cover. It means the sum insured should be assessed against the cost of treatment at the hospitals one is likely to use. A useful starting point is to examine the cost of common major hospitalisations in your city and consider whether your cover can absorb the expense of common procedures comfortably.The answer to this question also changes with your life stage and evolving needs. The distinction between an individual policy and a family floater can determine how much protection each member actually has. If a Rs 15 lakh family floater is shared by four members, it is a common pool and not Rs 15 lakh of dedicated cover for each person. If one member undergoes a major surgery, the remaining cover available to others reduces accordingly, subject to the policy’s benefits. A floater may work well for a young family with relatively similar healthcare needs, while individual policies may be worth considering when members are older or have different medical requirements. The decision should account for the family’s age profile, health history and the possibility of multiple claims in the same year.Urban India is seeing a rapid rise of lifestyle diseases, even among the young and healthy. So, factoring in pre-existing diseases and the waiting periods attached to them is important. In this regard, a higher sum insured does not automatically mean every medical expense will be covered from day one. Conditions such as diabetes, hypertension or thyroid disorders may be subject to specified waiting periods, depending on the policy.Consumers should disclose their medical history accurately and check when treatment related to a pre-existing condition becomes eligible for coverage. Buying insurance earlier, before such conditions develop, can help avoid some of these restrictions. For those who already have a diagnosis, there are plans available that waive off the waiting period for a small amount of additional premium.Here’s what most policyholders don’t understand - having a Rs 10 lakh policy does not necessarily mean getting the entire amount of an admissible Rs 10 lakh hospital bill. Why? Because copayment, voluntary deductible, room-rent cap and disease-specific sub-limits can leave the policyholder bearing the part of the cost. For example, a policy with a 20% copayment would require the insured to bear Rs 2 lakh of a Rs 10 lakh admissible claim, before accounting for any other applicable restrictions. Consumers should therefore examine the policy’s conditions alongside the headline cover amount. Employer-provided insurance should also be assessed in this context, particularly if it is the family’s only protection or may cease when employment ends.In a nutshell, assess your age and life-stage. But the objective is not to buy the largest policy available or chase a particular number. The purpose of the policy is to cover is adequate for the medical costs you could face and that its terms do not leave you with an unexpected financial burden. A review of these factors becomes especially important at major life transitions, when both healthcare needs and financial responsibilities can change.
Article Summary: There isn’t a single universal magic number that’s fit for everyone. Age is a useful starting point, but adequate health cover is determined by a combination of healthcare costs, family circumstances and the terms of the policy itself. A higher sum insured does not automatically mean every medical expense will be covered.

Article Title: On your mark, get set, go: Delhi to get Rs 100cr sports hostel and complex at Pitampura by April 2027
Article Text:
A new sports hostel and complex will be constructed in Pitampura by the Delhi government (Representative image)





NEW DELHI: Delhi govt will construct a sports hostel and complex at Pitampura at a cost of Rs 99.5 crore to provide year-round training infrastructure and residential facilities for budding athletes.The complex, being built on a 2.8-acre plot, will include an all-weather FINA-compliant swimming pool, a practice pool, gymnastics halls and residential facilities for 412 athletic students, including boys and girls.The project, bringing residential accommodation and specialised training infrastructure together, also marks a shift from seasonal sports facilities, an official said, adding that the financial approval has been given by Delhi govt. It would be completed by next April.The swimming pool, earlier planned as a basic open-air seasonal facility, has been upgraded to an indoor, climate-regulated arena with active heat-pump systems and long-span steel structure roofing, he said.The girls' hostel will be a ground-plus-seven-floor block with 96 rooms, six dormitories, a kitchen, a dining facility and recreational spaces. The boys' hostel, also a G+7 block, will have 76 rooms, six dormitories, a kitchen, a dining area, a multipurpose hall, indoor games and recreational zones.Both wings will be separately secured.An additional practice swimming pool will facilitate concurrent - resistance and aerobic or cardiovascular training - coaching. Two gymnastics training halls, including single- and double-height spaces, will be located on the first floor. The centre will also function as a centre for excellence for swimming.The complex will have a centralised solar power generation plant, an underground water tank and dedicated pool filtration plants, besides a 40KL D sewage treatment-cum-effluent treatment plant. Other infrastructure includes a high-definition CCTV security system, electricity sub-station and a backup DG set.Residential facilities will also be provided to budding athletes undergoing football, basketball, handball, volleyball and athletics training at other govt centres in the vicinity.
Article Summary: Delhi govt will construct a sports hostel and complex at Pitampura at a cost of Rs 99.5 crore. The complex, being built on a 2.8-acre plot, will include an all- weather FINA-compliant swimming pool, gymnastics halls and residential facilities.

Article Title: JEE Advanced 2026: 97 of top 100 rankers choose just 3 IITs; check which ones
Article Text:
IIT Bombay, IIT Delhi, and IIT Madras (pic) accounted for 97 of the top 100 JEE-Advanced rankers in 2026

Women’s success rate hits record high

SC, ST qualification rises sharply





NEW DELHI: IIT Bombay IIT Delhi and IIT Madras continued to dominate the choices of the country’s top JEE-Advanced rankers in 2026, with 97 of the top 100 rankers allotted seats at these three institutes. IIT Bombay alone accounted for 68 of the top 100, while IIT Delhi and IIT Madras took the remaining 29.Among the top 25 rankers, eight each took admission in IIT Delhi and IIT Madras, while six joined IIT Bombay.A total of 18,861 admissions were made across IITs, with women accounting for 3,814, or about 20.2%, according to the Joint Implementation Committee report prepared by IIT Roorkee. This was only a marginal increase from 20.15% the previous year.Women’s success rate in JEE-Advanced reached a record high in 2026 despite a decline in registrations. Of the 43,112 women registered, 10,107 qualified, taking their success rate to 23.4%, compared with 21.7% in 2025.Last year, 9,404 women had qualified from 43,413 registrations. Among women who appeared in both papers this year, the success rate was higher at 24.9%.However, women continued to account for a smaller share of qualifiers than their share of registrations.They made up 23% of registrations but only 17.8% of qualifiers.The number of women receiving IIT seat allotments rose from 3,664 in 2025 to 3,814 in 2026, an increase of about 4%. Of this year's allotments, 3,777 were in seats set aside exclusively for women and 37 were in seats open to all genders.IITs have been adding women-only seats to ensure that women account for at least one-fifth of new undergraduate students. Women are considered first for these seats within their respective categories.The report also shows a significant increase in the number of SC and ST candidates qualifying for JEE-Advanced.The number of SC qualifiers rose from 12,528 to 15,856, while the number of ST qualifiers increased from 5,017 to 6,379. Both rose by around 27%, much faster than the overall 4.6% increase in qualifiers, from 54,378 to 56,880.Including candidates with disabilities in both years, the qualification rate among registered candidates increased by 9.9 percentage points for SC candidates to 50.2%, and by 8.3 percentage points for ST can
Article Summary: IIT Bombay, IIT Delhi, and IIT Madras accounted for 97 of the top 100 JEE- Advanced rankers in 2026. Women’s success rate hits record high despite decline in registrations. SC, ST qualification rises sharply.
